newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Shots and teargas at Kinshasa march.
newsitem.headline: Shots and teargas at Kinshasa march.

text.p: Shots rang out in Zaire's capital Kinshasa on Wednesday as security forces tried to break up a march by thousands of supporters of new prime minister Etienne Tshisekedi, witnesses said.

Security forces were battling Tshisekedi supporters who turned out to accompany the veteran opposition leader and foe of President Mobutu Sese Seko to the prime minister's offices where he planned to install himself with his team.
Witnesses reported shooting after the crowd broke through a cordon of security forces who were blocking the approaches to the prime minister's offices.
Tshisekedi himself, tears streaming down his face from the teargas, walked in the direction of the offices. Armoured vehicles blocked the way further down the road.
Mobutu, who seized power in 1965 but has seen his hold over the sprawling country crumble as rebels advance, announced the state of emergency via a decree read on state television late on Tuesday.
He appointed military governors to Kinshasa and other areas not under rebel control.
